subject: Stellar Labs - evidence summary and confirmation of no customer data access
messages:
From: Alex Rutherford <alex.rutherford@stellarlabs.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@stellarlabs.com
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:12:31 -0700
Subject: Strange outbound traffic around May 17 - can you confirm?

Hi Jasmine,

We saw anomalous outbound connections from a host in our account around 2027-05-17 02:00 UTC (attached screenshot). It looks like multiple small POSTs to external endpoints over ~10 minutes and our security team flagged it as potential exfiltration. Can you confirm whether any customer data could have been read or streamed out of Redwood during that window? At minimum we need a short statement we can include in our internal report while we wait for a full postmortem.

Affected projects: stellarlabs/recommendation, stellarlabs/feature-store (both in us-west-2).

Thanks,
Alex
Senior SRE, Stellar Labs

Attachment: alert_screenshot.png (PNG)
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rutherford <alex.rutherford@stellarlabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:40:02 -0700
Subject: Re: Strange outbound traffic around May 17 - can you confirm?

Hi Alex — thanks for the alert and screenshot. I’ve looped in Marissa (CS) and Vivek (security/infra) to run an immediate integrity check. High level: we will 1) cross-check our access logs and transfer records for the stated time window, 2) compute file/object hashes for relevant storage buckets and compare to pre-incident snapshots, and 3) capture a chain-of-custody bundle for any artifacts we review.

We’ll aim to give you a preliminary statement within 48 hours and a full evidence package within 72 hours. Can you confirm the full list of API keys/service accounts used by those projects so we can narrow the audit scope?

— Jasmine
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Rutherford <alex.rutherford@stellarlabs.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 11:05:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Strange outbound traffic around May 17 - can you confirm?

Alex / team — quick interim findings from our forensics run this morning: 

- Scope: verified logs for us-west-2 accounts for the time window 2027-05-17 01:45 UTC to 2027-05-17 03:30 UTC.
- Network: the outbound POSTs in your screenshot match standard telemetry forwarding from a short-lived GPU worker that experienced a crash-restart loop. All destinations resolved to internal telemetry endpoints we operate; none of the egresses hit third-party endpoints outside our telemetry aggregation domain.
- Storage: we reconciled S3 object access logs and did a hash crosswalk against our archived snapshots. No object contents in your buckets were read outside of recorded customer requests. Hash differences we saw correspond to scheduled snapshot rotation (documented) — not external reads.
- Model serving: the incident caused a small number of cache evictions and re-materializations of model KV cache for ephemeral workers. These operations use in-memory transient state; they do not persist customer payloads.

I’ve attached the hash summary CSV (log-hash-summary-20270521.csv) and an internal notes PDF (forensic-notes-20270521.pdf). We are happy to share the full chain-of-custody bundle under NDA if you prefer.

Preliminary conclusion: no evidence of customer data exfiltration or unauthorized reads. We will finalize the timeline and produce a signed statement once the detailed bundle is complete.

— Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Infra Security, Redwood Inference

Attachment: log-hash-summary-20270521.csv (CSV)
From: Alex Rutherford <alex.rutherford@stellarlabs.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 12:18:44 -0700
Subject: Re: Strange outbound traffic around May 17 - can you confirm?

Thanks Vivek — that’s helpful. Two asks while you finalize: 1) our auditors need an explicit one-paragraph statement we can share that says whether customer data was accessed/exfiltrated during the event, and 2) we need a link or artifact showing the hash reconciliation results so we can attach them to our compliance ticket.

If you can provide a short signed PDF that we can include with our audit, that would close this loop from our side.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.
— Alex
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rutherford <alex.rutherford@stellarlabs.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 May 2027 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Strange outbound traffic around May 17 - can you confirm?

Alex — attaching the formal confirmation and the full evidence bundle reference. Summary below to use in your audit/report.

Official summary (for audit):
Redwood Inference has completed log and storage integrity checks for the incident affecting Stellar Labs on 2027-05-17. We reconciled network flow logs, object access logs, worker lifecycle events, and archived snapshots. Hash reconciliation was performed against archived snapshots taken prior to the incident window. Based on our analysis, there is no evidence that any Stellar Labs customer data was accessed by an unauthorized third party or exfiltrated from Redwood Inference systems during the incident. The observable activity is consistent with internal telemetry forwarding and transient model-serving worker restarts causing in-memory cache re-materialization.

Artifacts provided: log-hash-summary-20270521.csv; forensic-notes-20270522.pdf; signed-no-exfiltration-statement.pdf
JIRA: JIRA-INC-4821
Drive folder (evidence): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/incident-20270519-stellar

If you need a formal letter on Redwood letterhead or a notarized statement for regulators, please let me know and we’ll escalate. We can also run an additional packet capture of the host in question if Stellar wants a parallel verification.

— Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
